title: Could AI help decide medals at the 2028 Olympics?
description:
The 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles might look a little bit different…because of the use of AI-assisted judging. Sports like gymnastics are already starting to use the technology to decide who gets to stand on the podium in the run-up to 2028, and other Olympic disciplines like dressage, freestyle skiing and snowboarding are exploring doing the same.

Governing bodies say that AI could help to make things fairer, making judgements more accurate and objective. But some athletes aren’t happy with the decision - and say that AI can’t judge the artistry of their sport.

BBC Sports Correspondent Laura Scott joins us to explain how the AI judging process could work, which sports might adopt it in the future and how it might impact the 2028 Olympics in LA. We hear from the Olympic vault bronze medallist Harry Hepworth, on his experience of AI-assisted judging systems at the last World Gymnastics Championships. And sports journalist Emma (@emmasunny___) shares her thoughts on how this could impact how we wtach sports in the future.

summaryEn: This episode of the BBC podcast What in the World explores the potential and challenges of using AI-assisted judging in major sports competitions, including the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Sports federations, particularly in gymnastics, are adopting AI technology to minimize human bias and objectively assess move difficulty ratings. However, athletes like Olympic vault bronze medalist Harry Hepworth express concern that current AI systems fail to account for human body mechanics and safety—such as slight leg bends needed to prevent injury—leading to unfairly downgraded scores and forcing competitors to alter their techniques. Experts also highlight AI's limitations in evaluating artistry and nuance, raising concerns about potential technology failures at major events.
